messages.body_html:
====================================================

Computational and Systems Neuroscience 2027 (Cosyne)

MAIN MEETING & WORKSHOPS
11 - 16 March 2027
Montreal, Canada

www.cosyne.org

====================================================


IMPORTANT DATES

Abstract submission is now open.
Abstract submission deadline: 18 October 2026

Workshop proposal submission is now open.
Workshop proposal submission deadline: 01 November 2026

UNDERGRADUATE travel grant applications are now open.
UNDERGRADUATE travel grant submission deadline: 30 October 2026


----------------------------------------------------
COSYNE MEETING & WORKSHOPS
----------------------------------------------------

The annual Cosyne meeting provides an inclusive forum for the exchange of empirical and theoretical approaches to problems in systems neuroscience, in order to understand how neural systems function.

The MAIN MEETING is single-track. A set of invited talks is selected by the Executive Committee, and additional talks and posters are selected by the Program Committee, based on submitted abstracts. The WORKSHOPS feature in-depth discussion of current topics of interest, in a small group setting.

Cosyne topics include but are not limited to: neural basis of behavior, sensory and motor systems, circuitry, learning, neural coding, natural scene statistics, dendritic computation, neural basis of persistent activity, nonlinear receptive field mapping, representations of time and sequence, reward systems, decision-making, synaptic plasticity, map formation and plasticity, population coding, attention, neuromodulation, and computation with spiking networks.

We would like to foster increased participation from experimental groups as well as computational ones. Please circulate widely and encourage your students and postdocs to apply.

When preparing an abstract, authors should be aware that not all abstracts can be accepted for the meeting. Abstracts will be selected based on the clarity with which they convey the substance, significance, and originality of the work to be presented.


-----------------------------------------------------
CALL FOR WORKSHOP PROPOSALS
-----------------------------------------------------

A series of workshops will be held after the main Cosyne meeting. The goal is to provide an informal forum for the discussion of important research questions and challenges. Controversial issues, open problems, comparisons of competing approaches, and alternative viewpoints are encouraged.

Workshop proposals deadline: 01 November 2026
***To submit your Cosyne 2027 Workshop Proposal, please visit Cosyne.org -> Workshops -> Call for Proposals***

The overarching goal of all workshops should be the integration of empirical and theoretical approaches, in an environment that fosters collegial discussion and debate.

- There will be 6-10 workshops/day, running in parallel.
- Each workshop is expected to draw between 15 and 80 people.
- The workshops will be split into morning and late afternoon sessions.
- Workshops will be held in Montreal, Canada.
- Workshop speakers do NOT receive free registration, travel expenses, or accommodation for either the main meeting or the workshop sessions. Organizers should let invited speakers know that they are expected to pay for workshop registration fees.

Workshop organizer responsibilities include coordinating workshop participation and content, scheduling all speakers, submitting a final schedule for the workshop program, and moderating the discussion. Organizers can, but need not, be speakers. One complimentary (free) organizer registration is provided per workshop. For workshops with two organizers, the free registration can be given to one of the organizers or split evenly between them.

Any required multimedia resources beyond a projector, screen, and microphones will be the responsibility of the workshop organizers to coordinate with Cosyne and the workshop venue A/V staff.

EVALUATION CRITERIA

As stated above, the goal of Cosyne workshops is to provide an interactive, informal forum for discussions. Relevant topics include, but are not limited to: sensory processing; motor planning and control; functional neural circuits; motivation, reward and decision making; learning and memory; adaptation and plasticity; neural coding; neural circuitry and network models; and methods in computational or systems neuroscience.

Workshop proposals will be evaluated by the Cosyne Workshop Chairs, and a subset of the proposals will be selected. The proposals will be evaluated according to the following six metrics (which will be weighted equally):

- Relevance to the Cosyne community
- Integration of experimental and theoretical issues
- Current interest in the topic in the scientific community
- Potential for new research directions and interactions to emerge
- Distinctive scope/approach compared to other workshops (including previous years’)
- Diversity and equity in the proposed speaker (we are looking for representation of women or nonbinary individuals, individuals from other underrepresented groups, and a balance of established and early career researchers)

In order to foster discussion within Workshops and reduce overlap between workshops, organizers should inform invited speakers that a speaker can take part in no more than two Workshops.

WORKSHOP PROPOSAL

Each workshop proposal will include:
- Name(s) and email address(es) of the organizers (2 organizers per session is strongly recommended, but 3 will be allowed).
- A title.
- A brief description of 1. what the workshop will address and accomplish, 2. why the topic is of interest, 3. who is the targeted group of participants.
- Names and email addresses of speakers, who should already have agreed to participate should the proposal be accepted.
- Only proposals for one-day workshops will be accepted. The Workshop Chairs reserve the right to ask two workshops to merge into a two-day workshop, should topics align.
- A brief resume of the workshop organizer(s) along with a short list of workshop-relevant publications (about half a page total).
- A description of how you have addressed diversity and equity in your workshop.

Experience has shown that the best discussions during a workshop are those that arise spontaneously. A good way to foster these is to have short talks and long question periods (e.g. 30+15 minutes), and to have plenty of breaks. We recommend keeping the number of talks small (i.e., fewer than 10 talks per day).

WORKSHOP COSTS

Detailed registration costs, etc, will be at www.cosyne.org. Please note: Cosyne does NOT provide travel funding for workshop speakers. Organizers should let invited speakers know that they are expected to pay for workshop registration fees. Participants are encouraged to register early, in order to qualify for discounted registration rates. One complimentary (free) organizer registration is provided per workshop. For workshops with two organizers, the free registration can be given to one of the organizers or split evenly between them.

COSYNE 2027 WORKSHOP CHAIRS
Workshop Chairs: N Alex Cayco Gajic (ENS) and Marcelo Mattar (NYU)

COSYNE WORKSHOPS CONTACT
workshops [at] cosyne.org


-----------------------------------------------------
COSYNE TRAVEL GRANTS
-----------------------------------------------------

The COSYNE community is committed to bringing talented scientists together at our annual meeting, regardless of their ability to afford travel. Thus, a number of travel grants will be awarded to students, postdocs, and PIs for travel to the COSYNE meeting.

We currently offer five travel grant programs: Childcare, Presenters, New Attendees, Mentorship, and Undergraduate Travel Grants, see Cosyne.org -> Attend -> Travel Grants for details.

Applicants may apply for more than one grant program, but no applicant will receive more than one award. You may apply for a travel grant before receiving notification about the outcome of your submission. You may also apply if you are not submitting anything to the Main Meeting but still wish to attend Cosyne 2027.

messages.title: Open PhD and postdoc positions in computational neuroscience/neuroAI
messages.body_html:
Dear all,


We are inviting applications for the following collaborative PhD and postdoc positions in computational neuroscience/neuroAI:


  • PhD (based at TU Dresden, Germany): https://nextcloud.tuebingen.mpg.de/index.php/s/wbpcYQ5pgMjDJos

  • Postdoc (based at the Max Planck Institute for Biological Cybernetics, Germany): https://nextcloud.tuebingen.mpg.de/index.php/s/wjKjAHRidF5R4M8


We, the Natural Decision Making Group and the Natural Embodied Behavior Group, are joining forces within the CMC Unit to uncover the computational, biological, and ecological principles underlying adaptive decision-making. We combine computational methods from reinforcement learning, dynamical systems, and AI with analyses of neural and behavioral data to investigate how different species adapt their decisions to the dynamics of their natural environments, while accommodating their embodied constraints. 


We would appreciate it if you could share these calls with anyone who might be interested in your network.


Best wishes,

Shervin and Roxana

messages.title: Kosice Neuroscience Workshop, 19 - 21 April, 2027
messages.body_html:
SAVE THE DATE

The 6th workshop on

Cognitive neuroscience of auditory and cross-modal perception

19 - 21 April 2027, Košice (pronounced KOH-shih-tse), Slovakia
https://pcl.upjs.sk/workshop-2024

Objectives:

  • The workshop centers on how people perceive, attend to, and understand sounds—especially speech—in complex spatial, noisy, multimodal, and technologically mediated environments.
  • It aims to connect basic auditory mechanisms with real-world listening applications, using innovative tools such as games, mobile measures, neuroimaging, modeling, virtual environments, and hearing technologies. 
  • It will include advanced research talks (and introductory lectures) on a range of topics related to the neural processes of auditory, visual and cross-modal perception.
  • The workshop is aimed at early-stage and advanced students and young researchers, and it will provide ample opportunities for direct interactions between the lecturers and the attendees.

The workshop will follow up on our previous workshops. 

Guest speakers and SAV consortium speakers (tentative)

Inyong Choi, University of Iowa, United States
Norbert Vanek, University of Auckland, New Zealand
Eleni Vlahou, University of Thessaly, Greece
Mathieu Lavandier, ENTPE - University of Lyon France
Robert Baumgartner, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria
Piotr Majdak, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria
Anja Pahor, Univerza v Mariboru, Slovenia
Jyrki Ahveninen, Mass General Research Institute / Harvard Medical School, United States
Virginia Best; Boston University, United States
Aaron Seitz, Northeastern University, United States
Norbert Kopco, P. J. Šafárik University in Košice, Slovakia

Registration:

The workshop is open to all interested students/scientists. Registration is free of charge but required. To register, please send an email to EMAIL_REDACTED stating your full name and affiliation and the dates on which you are planning to attend. All accepted abstracts will be published on the workshop website and in the abstract book. No proceedings will be published. In case you would like to have a presentation please send us an abstract (up to 200 words; also indicate whether you prefer poster or oral presentation) no later than February 1, 2027. Also, see travel grant info below.

Student travel grants:

We offer a limited number of travel awards of 250 EUR to offset the cost of attending for students and young researcher. To apply, you need to be a presenting author. Please also introduce yourself and describe your motivation / reasons you need the travel grant.

Organizers:

Norbert Kopco, P. J. Šafárik University in Košice
Eleni Vlahou, University of Thessaly
Frederick Gallun, Oregon Health and Science University
Robert Baumgartner, Austrian Academy of Sciences
Piotr Majdak, Austrian Academy of Sciences
Mathieu Lavandier, ENTPE – University of Lyon
Aaron Seitz, Northeastern University
Perception and Cognition Lab

Acknowledgement:

The project has received funding from the HORIZON-MSCA-2022-SE-01 call (MSCA Staff Exchanges) of the research and innovation programme of Horizon Europe under the Marie Sklodowska-Curie actions grant agreement N° 101129903.

Sponsorship:

Organization of the workshop has been partially supported by the European Acoustics Association.

messages.title: GCNU-SWC Joint PhD Programme: Applications now open!
messages.body_html:
Gatsby Unit and Sainsbury Wellcome Centre Joint PhD Programme

Deadline: 17:00 GMT, Monday 9 November 2026

This four-year joint PhD programme, launched by the Gatsby Computational Neuroscience Unit (GCNU) and Sainsbury Wellcome Centre for Neural Circuits and Behaviour (SWC), aims to bridge the gap between theory and experiment. The programme immerses students in both experimental and theoretical thinking, providing rigorous training in a supportive environment for an interdisciplinary research career in academia or industry. First-year courses provide a comprehensive introduction to systems neuroscience, theoretical/computational neuroscience and machine learning. Students will be part of a broader trainee cohort across both centres, interacting and engaging in scientific discussion with both SWC and GCNU researchers with equal emphasis.

GCNU and SWC provide a unique opportunity to bring together a critical mass of theoreticians and experimentalists, fostering close interaction both among themselves and with researchers in the ELLIS Unit at UCL and across related UCL departments and domains, such as UCL Neuroscience Domain; Artificial Intelligence; Computer Science; Statistical Science; as well as researchers at the nearby Francis Crick Institute.

The applicants should have a strong analytical and mathematical background, a keen interest in neuroscience, and a relevant first degree (e.g., in Computer Science, Cognitive Psychology, Engineering, Mathematics, Neuroscience, Physics, Statistics).

Full funding is available regardless of nationality. We also welcome applicants who have secured, or are seeking, funding from other sources.

More information on the joint programme (including the key differences between the three PhD programmes offered by GCNU and SWC) and details on how to apply can be found on https://www.ucl.ac.uk/life-sciences/gatsby/study-and-work/gcnu-swc-joint-phd-programme.

--
I-Chun Lin, PhD
Scientific Programme Manager
Gatsby Computational Neuroscience Unit, UCL

topics.title: Fully funded PhD positions in computational neuroscience : modeling the complexity of neural oscillations
topics.snippet: Dear Colleagues, Fully funded PhD positions are available in my group at the Lyon Neuroscience

messages.author: Matteo di Volo
messages.title: Fully funded PhD positions in computational neuroscience : modeling the complexity of neural oscillations
messages.body_html:
Dear Colleagues,

Fully funded PhD positions are available in my group at the Lyon Neuroscience Research Center (CRNL), Lyon 1 University, starting in early 2027.

The project (Modeling the Complexity of Neural Oscillations, MoCoNo) studies how oscillatory patterns in prefrontal cortex support cognition, and which circuit mechanisms generate them. It combines analysis of electrophysiological recordings with biophysical computational models of cortical circuits.

We are looking for candidates with a Master's in computational neuroscience, physics, mathematics, computer science or a related field, strong programming skills, and an interest in data analysis or modelling.

To apply, send a CV, a short motivation letter and the names of two referees to EMAIL_REDACTED before 31 October 2026. For more information about the project, feel free to contact me at the same address.

Best regards,
Matteo Di Volo


--------

Prof. Matteo Di Volo
University Claude Bernard  Lyon1
https://matteodivolo.wordpress.com/

Master 2 Computational Neurosciences https://masterneuro.univ-lyon1.fr/m2-cns/

messages.author: Carmelo Bellardita
messages.title: [Postdoc] Neural Circuits of Sensorimotor Control – University of Copenhagen
messages.body_html:
Dear colleagues,

I am recruiting a postdoctoral researcher to join the Bellardita Lab at the Department of Neuroscience, University of Copenhagen.

The project investigates how neural circuits generate and adapt movement, combining experimental systems neuroscience with quantitative behaviour and computational analysis.

We are particularly interested in candidates with a background in systems, circuit or behavioural neuroscience. Relevant experience may include in vivo neural recordings or imaging, optogenetic/genetic manipulation, quantitative behavioural analysis, neural data analysis, or related computational approaches.

Postdoc in Neural Circuits of Sensorimotor Control
Bellardita Laboratory
Department of Neuroscience, University of Copenhagen
Copenhagen, Denmark

Duration: 2 years
Start: 1 January 2027 or by agreement
Application deadline: 14 October 2026

Full description and application:
https://employment.ku.dk/all-vacancies/?show=169394

I would be very grateful if you could share this opportunity with potentially interested candidates.

Best wishes,

Carmelo Bellardita
Associate Professor
Department of Neuroscience
University of Copenhagen

topics.title: Collaborative Postdoc position - Francis Crick Institute - University College London
topics.snippet: Hi all, I wanted to share an exciting postdoctoral opportunity jointly involving Florencia

messages.author: Sarah
messages.title: Collaborative Postdoc position - Francis Crick Institute - University College London
messages.body_html:
Hi all,

I wanted to share an exciting postdoctoral opportunity jointly involving Florencia Iacaruso’s lab at the Francis Crick Institute and my lab at University College London.

The project will investigate how neuromodulatory systems shape sensorimotor transformations in the superior colliculus, combining circuit neuroscience, behaviour and in vivo recordings/imaging across our two labs.

We’d be very keen to hear from motivated candidates with relevant expertise in systems or circuit neuroscience, particularly those interested in visual processing, sensorimotor transformations and neuromodulation.

More details and the application link are here:
https://www.crick.ac.uk/careers-study/vacancies/2026-09-24-neuromodulatory-control-of-sensorimotor-transformations-in-the-superior-colliculus

Please feel free to share with anyone who might be interested, and we’d be very happy to hear from potential applicants.

Best wishes,
Sarah

Sarah Ruediger 
Assistant Professor
Wellcome Trust CDA Fellow 
Department of Neuroscience, Physiology and Pharmacology 
University College London

topics.snippet: New York University is home to a thriving interdisciplinary community of researchers using

messages.author: Eero Simoncelli
messages.title: Doctoral studies in Computational/Theoretical Neuroscience at NYU
messages.body_html:
New York University is home to a thriving interdisciplinary community of researchers using computational and theoretical
approaches in neuroscience. We are interested in exceptional PhD candidates with strong quantitative training (e.g.,
physics, mathematics, engineering) coupled with a clear interest in scientific study of the brain.

A listing of faculty, sorted by their primary departmental affiliation, is given below.  Doctoral programs are flexible,
allowing students to pursue research across departmental boundaries. Nevertheless, admissions are handled separately by
each department, and students interested in pursuing graduate studies should submit an application to the program that
best fits their goals and interests.

Center for Neural Science (CNS), Graduate School of Arts & Sciences (deadline: 1 December)
[https://as.nyu.edu/cns/DoctoralProgram.html,  https://neuroscience.nyu.edu/program.html]
* Andre A. Fenton - Molecular, neural, behavioral, and computational aspects of memory.
* David Heeger (also in Psychology) - Computational neuroscience, vision, attention.
* Roozbeh Kiani - Vision and decision-making.
* Wei Ji Ma (also in Psychology) - Perception, working memory, and decision-making.
* Tony Movshon - Vision and visual development.
* Alex Reyes - Functional interactions of neurons in a network.
* John Pearson - Development, structure and function of sensory systems.
* John Rinzel (also in Mathematics) - Biophysical mechanisms and theory of neural computation.
* Cristina Savin (also in the Center for Data Science) - Computational models of learning and memory, machine learning.
* Robert Shapley - Visual physiology and perception.
* Eero Simoncelli (also in the FlatIron Institute) - Computational vision and audition.
* Xiao-Jing Wang - Computational neuroscience, decision-making and working memory, neural circuits.
* Alex Williams (also in the FlatIron Institute) - Statistical analysis of neural data.

Neuroscience Institute, School of Medicine (deadline: 1 December)
[https://med.nyu.edu/departments-institutes/neuroscience/,    https://neuroscience.nyu.edu/program.html]
* Gyorgy Buzsaki - Rhythms in neural networks.
* Zhe Chen - Memory and learning, cognitive flexibility and decision making, social behaviors, and pain.
* Dmitri Chklovskii (also in the FlatIron Institute) - Neural computation and connectomics.
* Paul W. Glimcher - Decision-making in humans and animals.  Neuroeconomics.
* Biyu He - Large-scale brain dynamics underlying human cognition.
* Dima Rinberg - Olfaction, sensory information processing, perception.
* Shy Shoham - Methods for controlling, imaging, and analyzing neural systems.
* Mario Svirsky - Auditory neural prostheses; experimental/computational studies of speech production/perception.

Psychology, Cognition & Perception program (deadline: 1 December)
[http://as.nyu.edu/psychology/graduate/phd-cognition-perception.html]
* Todd Gureckis - Memory, learning, and decision processes.
* Michael Landy - Computational approaches to vision.
* Laurence Maloney - Mathematical approaches to psychology and neuroscience.
* Marcelo Mattar - Learning and planning in the brain/mind.
* Denis Pelli - Visual object recognition.
* Jonathan Winawer - Visual perception and memory.

Data Science (deadline: 3 December)
[https://cds.nyu.edu/phd-program/]
* Joan Bruna (also in Computer Science) - Machine learning, signal/image processing.
* Kyungyun Cho (also in Computer Science) - Machine learning, natural language processing.
* Carlos Fernandez-Granda (also in Mathematics) - Optimization methods for medical imaging, neuroscience, computer vision.
* Brenden Lake (also in Psychology) - Computational modeling of cognition, deep learning.
* Grace Lindsay (also in Psychology) - Machine learning models of the brain/mind.
* Mengye Ren (also in Computer Science) - Brain and cognitively inspired representation learning.

Mathematics (deadline: 18 December)
[https://gsas.nyu.edu/admissions/arc/programs/mathematics.html]
* Aaditya Rangan -  Computational neurobiology, numerical analysis.
* Charles Peskin - Mathematical biology.
* Daniel Tranchina - Information processing in the retina.
* Lai-Sang Young - Dynamical systems, statistical physics, computational modeling and theoretical neuroscience.

Physics (deadline: 30 December)
[https://as.nyu.edu/physics/programs/graduate.html]
* Marc Gershow - Perception, decision-making, and learning in neural circuits.
* Stefano Martiniani - Fundamental principles governing neural systems.

Computer Science (deadline: 12 December)
[http://www.cs.nyu.edu/home/phd/]
* Davi Geiger - Computational vision and learning.
* Yann LeCun - Machine learning, computer vision, robotics, computational neuroscience.

Economics (deadline: 18 December)
[https://as.nyu.edu/econ/graduate/phd.html]
* Andrew Caplin - Economic theory, neurobiology of decision.
* Andrew Schotter - Experimental economics, game theory, neurobiology of decision.

topics.title: Re: 2 postdoc and 1 phD positions on computational mechanisms of human perception (Alex Hyafil & Chris Summerfield, Barcelona)
topics.snippet: The group of Alex Hyafil at the CRM Barcelona (https://ahyafil.github.io/) is looking for two postdoc

messages.author: Alexandre Hyafil
messages.title: Re: 2 postdoc and 1 phD positions on computational mechanisms of human perception (Alex Hyafil & Chris Summerfield, Barcelona)
messages.body_html:
The group of Alex Hyafil at the CRM Barcelona (https://ahyafil.github.io/) is looking for two postdoc researchers and a PhD student.  

One of the postdoc positions will be co-supervised by Chris Summerfield (Universitat Pompeu Fabra Barcelona / Oxford; https://humaninformationprocessing.com/). The selected candidate will investigate the computational operations underlying visual scene perception through a combination of simulation of artificial visual systems (conv nets, visual transformers) and human experiments. The position is for two years.

The other postdoc researcher (2-year duration) and the PhD student (4-year) will work jointly on identifying canonical Bayesian operations at play in human visual and auditory perception. The project involves Bayesian modelling, artificial vision network simulations, behavioral and EEG experiments as well as intra-cranial EEG experiments (in collaboration with Benjamin Morillon, AMU Marseille). We will look for complementarity of the two profiles, notably in terms of quantitative and experimental backgrounds.  

 

The hired researchers will benefit from the stimulating environment of the Barcelona area in cognitive and computational neuroscience. Our groups form part of a larger interacting network of neuroscience labs in Barcelona (http://www.barccsyn.org). Financial support is provided by the Spanish National Agency of Investigation (FPI fellowship for the PhD student).

 

APPLICATION: Send a curriculum and motivation letter with a list of two contacts for recommendation letter at https://bit.ly/ChrisAlexPositions. Informal enquiries are welcome.

DEADLINE: before October 31 for the PhD position; until position is filled for the postdoc positions.

STARTING DATE: before July 2027 for the PhD position; flexible for the postdoc positions

topics.title: Two-photon Microscopy Troubleshooting Workshop
topics.snippet: Dear colleagues, We are planning a workshop on Troubleshooting Two-Photon Microscopy in Biological

messages.author: Urszula Włodkowska
messages.title: Two-photon Microscopy Troubleshooting Workshop
messages.body_html:
Dear colleagues,

We are planning a workshop on Troubleshooting Two-Photon Microscopy in Biological Samples, organised by the Nencki Institute of Experimental Biology in collaboration with Nencki Open Lab.

The workshop is intended for researchers and imaging specialists who already have some hands-on experience with two-photon microscopy. It will help you get better at identifying and resolving technical and experimental problems, and show you how to customize and extend your setups.

Our aim is to bring together experts in optics, microscopy instrumentation and biological imaging to discuss common challenges, from microscope performance and image acquisition to sample preparation and optimisation of experimental conditions.
We would like to make the workshop as practical and relevant as possible, with discussions based on real imaging problems encountered by participants.
If you are interested, please complete this short survey to help us identify the topics and challenges you would most like us to address:
https://forms.gle/mNNPCJ8JmeCSCpTy5

Please feel free to share this invitation with colleagues who might be interested. In case of any questions, reach out to us at EMAIL_REDACTED or EMAIL_REDACTED.

topics.title: Funded PhD Opportunities at the University of Toronto: NeuroAI and Computational Neuroscience
topics.snippet: Funded PhD Opportunities: NeuroAI and Computational Neuroscience at the University of Toronto I am

messages.author: Helena Liu
messages.title: Funded PhD Opportunities at the University of Toronto: NeuroAI and Computational Neuroscience
messages.body_html:
Funded PhD Opportunities: NeuroAI and Computational Neuroscience at the University of Toronto


I am recruiting PhD students to join my new lab at the University of Toronto for Fall 2027. We study how brains and artificial neural networks learn from experience, form useful representations, assign credit to past events, and generalize to new situations. Our work combines computational neuroscience, machine learning, mathematical modeling, and neural and behavioral data, and has appeared in PNAS, NeurIPS, ICLR, and ICML.

Research directions include how biological mechanisms support learning from delayed feedback; how neural circuit structure and learning dynamics shape representations, generalization, and continual learning; and methods for inferring learning processes from neural and behavioral data. As one of the founding students, you can begin with a concrete project in one of these directions, with room to bring your own interests into the work and help shape the lab’s culture. You can learn more about our work at helena-yuhan-liu.github.io.

Who should apply: Students from computer science, engineering, statistics, physics, applied mathematics, neuroscience, psychology, and related fields are encouraged to apply. A strong quantitative background and experience with scientific programming are important; applicants should be comfortable with linear algebra, probability/statistics, and computational problem solving. Prior training in neuroscience or psychology is not required. We especially value students who are intellectually curious, creative, self-motivated, and able to take ownership of a project and carry it through to completion.

What we offer: Close, direct mentorship with individualized support for research and career development; interdisciplinary training in computational methods and scientific thinking; and opportunities to present at conferences and publish in machine-learning and neuroscience venues. Students will benefit from U of T’s strengths in AI, neuroscience, and cognitive science, with opportunities to connect and collaborate across disciplines. Toronto combines a vibrant research community with diverse neighborhoods, a lively arts scene, and excellent food.

Admission and funding: This is a funded PhD opportunity through U of T’s Psychology graduate program. The program uses direct admission to a supervisor’s lab. Direct entry from a bachelor’s degree is available for eligible applicants; applicants with a master’s degree are also welcome. The application deadline is December 1, 2026. Please see the program’s application page for application requirements and instructions.

Interested? Please apply through the U of T Psychology PhD program and list me as a prospective supervisor. If you have questions about research fit, feel free to email me with your CV attached.

Best,
Helena Liu
________________________________________
Y. Helena Liu
Postdoctoral Research Associate, Princeton University
Incoming Assistant Professor (January 2027), Department of Psychology, University of Toronto
Website: https://helena-yuhan-liu.github.io/

Our work combines computational neuroscience, machine learning, mathematical modeling, and neural and behavioral data, and has appeared in PNAS, NeurIPS, ICLR, and ICML.

Research directions include how biological mechanisms support learning from delayed feedback; how neural circuit structure and learning dynamics shape representations, generalization, and continual learning; and methods for inferring learning processes from
neural and behavioral data. As one of the founding students, you can begin with a concrete project in one of these directions, with room to bring your own interests into the work and help shape the lab’s culture. You can learn more about our work at

helena-yuhan-liu.github.io.

Who should apply: Students from computer science, engineering, statistics, physics, applied mathematics, neuroscience, psychology, and related fields are encouraged to apply. A strong quantitative background and experience with scientific programming
are important; applicants should be comfortable with linear algebra, probability/statistics, and computational problem solving. Prior training in neuroscience or psychology is not required. We especially value students who are intellectually curious, creative,
self-motivated, and able to take ownership of a project and carry it through to completion.

What we offer: Close, direct mentorship with individualized support for research and career development; interdisciplinary training in computational methods and scientific thinking; and opportunities to present at conferences and publish in machine-learning
and neuroscience venues. Students will benefit from U of T’s strengths in AI, neuroscience, and cognitive science, with opportunities to connect and collaborate across disciplines. Toronto combines a vibrant research community with diverse neighborhoods, a
lively arts scene, and excellent food.

Admission and funding: This is a funded PhD opportunity through U of T’s Psychology graduate program. The program uses direct admission to a supervisor’s lab. Direct entry from a bachelor’s degree is available for eligible applicants; applicants with
a master’s degree are also welcome. The application deadline is December 1, 2026. Please see

the program’s application page for application requirements and instructions.

Interested? Please apply through the U of T Psychology PhD program and list me as a prospective supervisor. If you have questions about research fit, feel free to email me with your CV attached.

Best,

Helena Liu

________________________________________

Y. Helena Liu

Postdoctoral Research Associate, Princeton University

Incoming Assistant Professor (January 2027), Department of Psychology, University of Toronto

Website:
https://helena-yuhan-liu.github.io/

topics.snippet: Interested in a PhD or postdoc in computational neuroscience? Several openings are available at the

messages.author: Chris Cueva
messages.title: PhD and postdoctoral opportunities in computational neuroscience at the University of Colorado Anschutz
messages.body_html:
Interested in a PhD or postdoc in computational neuroscience? Several openings are available at the University of Colorado Anschutz.

The computational neuroscience community at CU Anschutz is expanding, with groups led by Nick Lesica, Tahra Eissa, Laureline Logiaco, and Christopher Cueva. Our research interests span neural dynamics and circuit modeling, behavioral modeling, neuro-AI, and model-guided closed-loop brain stimulation, across sensory, motor, and cognitive systems.

Our local experimental collaborators work on circuit manipulation in human and mice neurophysiology, creating opportunities at the intersection of computational and experimental neuroscience, with applications ranging from fundamental discovery to clinical neurostimulation.

We welcome inquiries from prospective PhD students and postdoctoral researchers interested in joining this growing community. Prospective postdoctoral candidates may also explore opportunities to visit CU Anschutz and present their research through CU Peaks. Prospective PhD students can apply through any of the following graduate programs by December 1 (November 1 priority deadline for international applicants):
  • Neuroscience Program (biology-focused)
  • Computational Bioscience Program (computationally focused)
  • Biomedical Engineering Program, with a Neuroengineering Certificate (engineering-oriented)

messages.title: 2nd UK Theoretical Neuroscience Workshop
messages.body_html:
We are pleased to announce the 2nd UK Theoretical Neuroscience Workshop, taking place at City St George’s, University of London, on Friday, 18 December 2026.

The workshop will bring together researchers and students working in theoretical, mathematical, and computational neuroscience and psychiatry for a day of invited talks, poster presentations, and discussion.

Venue: City St George’s, University of London
Date: Friday, 18 December 2026
Time: 09:00–18:10
Programme: Invited talks, poster sessions, discussions, and a poster award

Invited speakers include researchers from UCL, Oxford, Warwick, Nottingham, Birmingham, and Edinburgh, covering topics across neural dynamics, learning, network modelling, motor control, functional connectomics, temporal inference, and related areas.

Further information, including the programme and abstracts, is available

          Here 

Please feel free to circulate this announcement among interested colleagues and students.

Best wishes,
UK Theoretical Neuroscience Workshop Organisers

Professor Steve Coombes

Dr Dimitrios Pinotsis

topics.snippet: Dear colleagues, The Centre for Theoretical Neuroscience at the University of Waterloo is excited to

messages.author: Madeleine Bartlett
messages.title: [Meetings] Call For Applications 2027 Nengo Summer School
messages.body_html:
Dear colleagues,

The Centre for Theoretical Neuroscience at the University of Waterloo is excited to announce our 12th annual Nengo summer school on large-scale brain modelling and neuromorphic computing. This two-week school will teach participants to use the Nengo simulation package to build state-of-the-art cognitive and neural models to run both in simulation and on neuromorphic hardware. Summer school participants will be given on-site access to neuromorphic hardware and will learn to run high-level applications using Nengo! 


More generally, Nengo provides users with a versatile and powerful environment for designing cognitive and neural systems and has been used to build what is currently the world's largest functional brain model, Spaun, which includes spiking deep learning, reinforcement learning, adaptive motor control, and cognitive control networks. 


For a look at the last summer school, check out this short video: 

https://youtu.be/hHwIryt053M?si=N70eVlC3Sm_2sDy5 


We welcome applications from all interested graduate students, postdocs, professors, and industry professionals with a relevant background.


***Application Deadline: December 21st, 2026***


Format: A combination of tutorials and project-based work. Participants are encouraged to bring their own ideas for projects, which may focus on testing hypotheses, creating models to account for neural or cognitive data, implementing specific behavioural functions with neurons, expanding past models, or providing a proof-of-concept of various neural mechanisms. Hands-on tutorials, individual or group projects, and talks from invited faculty members will make up the bulk of day-to-day activities. A project demonstration event will be held on the last day of the school, with prizes for strong projects!


Participants will have the opportunity to learn how to:

  • interface Nengo with various kinds of neuromorphic hardware (e.g. BrainDrop, SpiNNaker)

  • build perceptual, motor, and sophisticated cognitive models using spiking neurons

  • build models to account for anatomical, electrophysiological, cognitive, and behavioural data

  • use a variety of single cell models within a large-scale model 

  • integrate machine learning methods into biologically oriented models

  • interface Nengo with cameras and robotic systems

  • implement modern nonlinear control methods in neural models

  • neurally implement vector symbolic architecture algorithms

  • and much more…


Date and Location: May 30th to June 11th, 2027 at the University of Waterloo, Ontario, Canada.


Applications: Please visit http://www.nengo.ai/summer-school, where you can find more information regarding costs, travel, lodging, along with an application form listing required materials.


If you have any questions about the school or the application process, please contact:

Madeleine Bartlett: EMAIL_REDACTED

Kathryn Simone: EMAIL_REDACTED 


The school is partly supported by ABR, Inc. 


We look forward to hearing from you!

Maddy
